A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RML research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RML results for clustering, noisy-label classification, and cross-modal retrieval, alongside ablations and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendix, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and convergence analyses.

M1.justification: The sample-level attention fusion network, simulated perturbations, contrastive objective, and downstream regularization procedures remain unchanged, including the task-specific formulations in Appendix 7.1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine clustering datasets, five noisy-label classification datasets, and MIRFLICKR-25K/NUS-WIDE retrieval tasks. The appendix retains the same noise-rate scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the clustering, classification, and retrieval comparisons. NRCH and RML+NRCH were already treated as a separate comparison in v1 Appendix 7.2.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, metrics, model settings, perturbation parameters, and hash lengths are unchanged. The more specific ablation captions disclose existing configurations without establishing a protocol change.

E4.justification: Table 5 and Figures 3–10 retain the same component ablations, perturbation-ratio and regularization-weight sensitivity analyses, and convergence evidence. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent runs for clustering and classification and provide the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Appendix Tables 7–9. No statistical procedure or uncertainty reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1 and 3–9, including appendix standard deviations, are identical, and the experimental plots are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports BDGP accuracy of 0.936 for RML+LMCE at 50% label noise in both versions.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–3 and Equations 1–19 are unchanged. The description of cosine similarity is corrected from distance-related wording, but its formula and mathematical reasoning remain the same.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about sample-level fusion, perturbation-based alignment, robustness, and applicability across the three downstream tasks.

C2.justification: Scientific interpretations and the societal-impact statement remain unchanged. The new Table 4 note repeats the NRCH comparability restriction already stated in v1 Appendix 7.2.

D1.justification: v2 adds an RML code repository link in the abstract. Captions also explicitly identify RML+LMCE for Table 5 and RML+UCCH for Figure 4; the implementation details and hyperparameters in Appendix 7 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added, including MetaQ, AugRefer, and Lukov et al. on noisy facial-expression labels. These expand supporting context without substantially revising the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording and grammar edits, updates affiliation numbering and corresponding-author markers, adds an acknowledgment, expands the appendix heading, and renames Section 5 to Conclusion. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table and figure captions gain clarifications, Table 4 gains a comparison note, and appendix material undergoes modest spacing and placement changes. All existing figures and tables are retained without substantive graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 provides code-access information, identifies the configurations used in existing ablations, and places the existing NRCH comparison restriction directly beside Table 4. These changes modestly improve documentation and reduce ambiguity, while the scientific methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
